PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called the meeting to order at 5:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on CLosed Session agenda. 

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council/Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:02 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:12 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items:

Item #1 (A, B, C, D): Staff provided a presentation, and the City Council gave direction. No reportable action was taken on these items.

Item #2: A presentation was provided by staff, followed by direction from the City Council. No reportable action was taken.

Item #3: Two matters of potential litigation were discussed. Staff presented, and the City Council provided direction. No reportable action was taken on these items.

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called regular meeting to order at 6:14 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Transportation Director McFerguson led the Pledge of Allegiance

INVOCATION Councilmember Rebollo offered the invocation. 

PUBLIC COMMENT Margarita Martinez expressed her gratitude to Sergeant Duarte for his exceptional assistance in resolving her issue and for going above and beyond in addressing her concerns.

Josie Betancourt emphasized the need for better outreach to residents regarding the recent restriping on Commerce Way. She also thanked the Parks and Recreation staff for their efforts in organizing a Dodgers game.

Gloria Nezahualcoyotl extended her appreciation to the Transportation Department for their efforts in restoring the bus routes to their previous state.

Rolando Ortiz spoke on behalf of a group of residents who utilize the handball courts at Bristow Park, requesting that the courts remain unchanged.








CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Mayor Argumedo stated that item #12 is conitnued to the next meeting.  Mayor Argumedo pulled item #4. 

Item #4 - After brief discussion, Councilmember Lainez moved, seconded by Councilmember Garcia, to adopt a resolution  accepting the Eastern Avenue Median Improvements Project as complete, authorizing staff to file the Notice of Completion with the County Recorder’s Office, and authorizing release of 5% retention per contract provisions.  The motion was carried by the following vote:

AYES: Councilmembers Garcia, Lainez, Rebollo, Vice Mayor Altamirano and Mayor Argumedo (5)

4.. Eastern Avenue Median Improvements Project Acceptance

3.. Letter of Opposition for SB 549 (Newman) Gaming: Tribal Nations Access to Justice Act

5.. State of Good Repair Funding Allocation for Fiscal Year 2024-2025

6.. Commerce Water System Rates - Continuation of PFAS Surcharge

7.. Approval of Agreement for Crossing Guard Services with All City Management Services

2.. Approval of Minutes

8.. Third Amendment to an Agreement  to Provide the City Maintenance and Support Services Related to the Transit Business Intelligent Software System

9.. Agreements for Executive Search Services for Vacant Finance Director and Public works Director Positions

1.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 2A, 24A, 2B and 24B

SCHEDULED MATTERS

12.. Transit Supervisor Position for the Transportation Department This item was continued to the next meeting. 

10.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE Sergeant Duarte provided an overview of the past two weeks, noting that the response times were below the average for the City of Commerce.

 Councilmember Lainez requested a breakdown of the response times for routine, priority, and emergency calls.



11.. Installation of Creative Artwork at the City’s Six Crosswalks  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo City Manager Hernandez provided an overview of the staff report.  

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Garcia reported that she attended the Scholarship Program and expressed gratitude to the library staff. She noted that the keynote speaker was particularly inspirational. Councilmember Garcia also attended National Night Out, praised the event's organization, and thanked the Public Safety staff. Additionally, she enjoyed the Concert in the Park and appreciated the Parks and Recreation Department for providing recycling bins.

Councilmember Rebollo thanked the Public Safety team for their efforts during National Night Out and expressed her gratitude to the sponsors who provided backpacks for students returning to school. While she was unable to attend the Scholarship Breakfast due to her participation in the Contract Cities meeting. Councilmember Rebollo wished her mother a Happy Birthday.

Councilmember Lainez reported on his attendance at the Scholarship Breakfast, where he congratulated all 39 recipients and thanked the donors and library staff for their coordination. Councilmember Lainez also attended National Night Out and extended his thanks to the staff for organizing the event. Councilmember Lainez mentioned attending a Dodgers game and praised the Parks Department's tailgate event at the Senior Center, which was well-received by attendees.

Vice Mayor Altamirano shared that National Night Out was a great event, especially with it being held at one park. He thanked the businesses that contributed.  Vice Mayor Altamirano acknowledged Councilmember Garcia for her dedication to promoting arts in public spaces, expressing hope that similar initiatives will be implemented in other areas of the city.

Mayor Argumedo reported attending the Scholarship Awards, National Night Out, Dodger Community Night, and the Concert in the Park. He also thanked those involved in organizing the tailgate party and took a moment to wish his son, Brandon, a Happy Birthday.

The meeting recessed to Closed Session at 6:53 p.m.











ADJOURNMENT City Council recessed from Closed Session at 8:19 p.m. and after oral Closed Session announcement, the City Council adjourned the meeting at 8:20 p.m.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.


Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.
